conventions.convention: Real suprema require nonempty bounded-above sets; real infima require nonempty bounded-below sets. Neither empty-set bound is defined in R.
Metrics and pseudometrics have finite real values. Separation, symmetry and the triangle inequality define metrics; pseudometrics replace separation by diagonal zero. Nonnegativity is derived.

Rational powers use positive roots and integer powers. At zero, the rational/integer regime assigns 0^0=1, while the separate real-power regime leaves 0^0 undefined. The positive square-root smoothness claim excludes zero.
Sequences are indexed by N starting at zero. The sequential limit criterion requires a limit point c and sequences avoiding c; only its reverse implication invokes indexed countable choice.

Geodesic completeness concerns maximal affine geodesics on boundaryless Riemannian manifolds. Metric completeness uses the induced distance componentwise; no Lorentzian Hopf–Rinow implication is supplied.
Indexed bundle data have a supplied set index. Tagged unions and quotients are constructed within products and power sets by Separation; definable classes are formula abbreviations.
The total extended product is a new operation assigning zero whenever either factor is zero, including infinite other factors; it does not redefine the supplier's partial extended arithmetic.

Lp elements are almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable real-valued representatives. Point values concern specified representatives. No completeness assumption on the measure or simultaneous representative choice is imposed.

Circle data use a supplied countable cover, g_ij g_jk=g_ik, a_j=a_i+df_ij, and fibre coordinates z_j=g_ij^(-1)z_i. The connection is locally η+a_i. The fixed positive normalization κ₀ has units Wb and F=κ₀ da_i.

Sphere flux uses outward orientation and increasing-angle circle orientations. North-to-south winding is −2b/κ₀, while normalized flux is +2b/κ₀. Flat holonomy is exp(−2πia). Integrality restricts the chosen circle normalization, not every classical flux.

load_bearing.statement: A normalized circle-connection datum consists of a supplied countable open cover, smooth circle transition maps satisfying the cocycle, compatible smooth real local one-forms with a_j=a_i+λ(g_ij), and a fixed κ₀>0; chart transfer is z_j=g_ij^(-1)z_i.

The stated normalized countable chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal U(1)-bundle and smooth real connection ω, with dω=π*f for a global smooth closed two-form f locally equal to da_i. Connections with the same transitions differ by a global base one-form.

For a smooth closed two-form on an open D⊆R⁴ star-shaped about p, A_b(x)=∫₀¹t(x−p)^a F_ab(p+t(x−p))dt defines a smooth one-form with dA=F. The analogous integral for a smooth closed one-form α defines smooth χ with dχ=α.

On the stated punctured Minkowski domain, F_b is smooth and closed with outward unit-sphere flux 4πb, and has no global potential when b≠0. Its north/south potentials admit the specified circle transition exactly when 2b/κ₀∈Z, with winding −2b/κ₀. The stated flat product-bundle connection has holonomy exp(−2πia) and is gauge trivial exactly when a∈Z.
For q>0, let s(q) be the unique positive root specified in def-emg-explicit-power-regimes. Then s:(0,∞)→(0,∞) is smooth and s′(q)=1/(2s(q)).

For supplied set-indexed local bundle data, the tagged union is a set, equivalence classes are subsets of it, and the quotient is formed by Separation within its power set, without choosing representatives.

concerns.concern: F3 says thm-algebra-of-derivatives 'gives the product and chain rules'. Its Statement gives sum, scalar, product and quotient rules, but no chain rule. The proof can differentiate s(q)s(q) using the product rule, so this is an inaccurate supplier attribution rather than an unsupported conclusion.

Step 2.1 defines c using R∘σ_j, but subsequently writes ∫_c F_b=Σ_j∫_{tilde σ_j}F_b=∫_{S²}F_b. The tilde σ_j still parametrize planar tetrahedron faces; the finite-parametrization supplier applies to R∘tilde σ_j. Retain R in those integral subscripts, or explicitly justify the additional radial pullback identity R*F_b=F_b. The intended orientation-preserving parametrizations have already been established, so the missing bridge is immediate.
